page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this arm64 architecture features 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per core, with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a massive 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, which correlates with exceptional database and key-value store performance, as evidenced by top-tier PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, and LLM text generation speeds are weak to poor, highlighting a clear tradeoff between massive parallel throughput and sequential execution or specialized AI inference workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i8g.metal-48xl offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage capacity with a high-core-count ARM architecture, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, static web serving, and parallelized software compilation. It is less suitable for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or GPU-accelerated machine learning tasks.
